human_tolerance.notes: Occurs in parks and wooded suburbs with mature trees; cavity nesting and tree-trunk foraging depend on tree cover.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: Most breeding reported from early May to early June; the source notes geographic variation.

vocalizations.description: Rapid nasal qui notes, associated with courtship and territory.
Repeated shrill kri notes increase with anxiety or excitement.

taxonomy.note: GBIF exact accepted species match; iNaturalist independently resolves the active species at species rank.

range.note: North American breeding range described as southern Canada through the United States to Mexico; country codes indicate native range, excluding vagrants.

habitat.note: Trunk and branch foraging, mature woodland, tree cavity nesting and occasional ground feeding; habitat fractions and resource weights are authored approximations.

behavior.note: Authored local bark-foraging FSM. Nuthatches move by jerky hops along trunks and branches, descend head-first, and occasionally feed on the ground. Climb has no dedicated rendered pose, so its pose is a stylized limitation.

vocalizations.note: Nasal song and contact/alarm calls summarized from the species article; timing and cooldowns are authored.

look.note: Palette follows the pale blue-gray upperparts, white underparts and dark crown described for males. Proportions and pose details are authored stylization.

traits.mass_kg.note: Midpoint of the article range 18-30 g: (18+30)/2=24 g, converted to 0.024 kg. This is a simple range midpoint, not a measured species mean.

traits.length_m.note: Midpoint of the article range 13-14 cm: (13+14)/2=13.5 cm, converted to 0.135 m.

traits.lifespan_y.note: The article states an estimated average lifespan of two years and distinguishes it from the 12-year-9-month banding record. ADW Lifespan/Longevity section was checked and says the same two-year wild estimate, but was not used because its text licence is CC BY-NC-SA 3.0; the permissively licensed article provides the estimate and cites its source.

activity.US.note: GBIF tier A, country-level US query; 12,363,538 observations; all twelve monthly bins usable. iNaturalist tier C returned zero and was not used. Activity is observation frequency, not direct abundance.

seasonal.strategy.note: The species article describes it as non-migratory, with adults normally remaining in territory year-round.

seasonal.phases.note: Geographic Range section: most breeding early May to early June, with some regional variation; phase represents that broad typical US window.

seasonal.life_stages.note: Stages are listed without duration because the published fledging range varies.
